adversary_breaks.expected: A backwards wall-clock jump cannot extend a lease: the reading after resume must be rollbackDetected=true (reconcile_required/clock_rollback) or prove expiry — never 'active'. Root cause is structural: performance.now() does not count suspended time and the module has no sleep-inclusive monotonic source (e.g. the iOS continuous/boot clock that packages/shared-types OfflineNativeTimeEvidence describes), so a frozen monotonic interval is indistinguishable from 'no time passed'.
adversary_breaks.observed: VERIFIED: after an authenticated anchor, the app is backgrounded, the device sleeps 6 days (wall advances, performance.now() frozen) and the wall clock is wound back BEFORE the app returns to the foreground; the foreground checkpoint then runs against the already-rewound clock, read() returns authority='anchored', rollbackDetected=false, nowMs ≈ anchor+1 min, and evaluateLease(1-day lease) returns kind='active'. Repeating 10x (2 days sleep + rollback each cycle) keeps a 7-day lease 'active' after 20 real days (seen.slice(-3) = [1,1,1]). The candidate's own 'device sleep' test (w05TrustedTime.test.ts:361) only covers the order honest-foreground THEN rollback; the attack suite's boundary test confirms that order IS caught. On iOS the user must leave the app to reach Settings > Date & Time, so rollback-while-suspended is the realistic order.

breaks.observed: VERIFIED on c735b23d. 1a: anchored at T0 in foreground, 1 min of use, app goes inactive->background, process clock frozen for 6 honest days, app returns to 'active'; the foreground checkpoint reads nowMs = T0+6d+60s (floor, not active). Then an authenticated response whose Date header is T0+1m+2s (the request that was in flight when the phone locked) is fed via observeServerTime exactly as api.ts does for every bearer response. observeServerTime: accepted=true; the next read() returns nowMs = 1788868863000 (T0+1m+3s) versus 1789387260000 before delivery -> trusted time moved BACKWARDS by ~6 days inside one process, authority='anchored', continuity='measured'. 1b: same sequence with the wall clock wound back to T0+1m while suspended: before the stale response evaluateLease -> {reconcile_required, elapsed_unmeasured} (correct); after it evaluateLease(7-day lease) -> 'active' with ~7 days remaining although 6 real days elapsed and the clock was rolled back. Cause (INFERRED from trustedTime.ts observeServerTime): `inForeground`/`leavesAtCall` are sampled at CALL time (after resume, app is 'active', foregroundLeaves unchanged) and anchorMs = max(serverEpochMs, anchorEstimateMs(at)) where the estimate after suspension is only anchor+frozen-monotonic ≈ T0+1m; the persisted/current floor (T0+6d) is not consulted, and `floor = null` discards it. The module has no notion of when the REQUEST was sent, so a response received after resume is treated as fresh foreground evidence. Realism: the response bytes can be held by the network (slow cellular, or a TCP-level delay by a router the user controls — no TLS break needed) and are delivered by NSURLSession when the process resumes; api.ts only enforces its own 20 s deadline via a JS timer whose ordering against the resolved fetch on resume is UNKNOWN on Linux.

implement.approach: Regression tests first (663bc0ee, 8486e706), then the fix (c735b23d). The module keeps r2's sound parts — authenticated `Date`-header anchoring via api.ts, forward-carry on the process monotonic clock, in-process ratcheting high-water mark, device-only Keychain floor (`com.picklesensei.offline.trusted-time`, AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY, cloudSync:false), 5-minute rollback tolerance, 7-day lease cap — and adds elapsed-time *continuity*: an anchor is 'measured' only while the app has stayed in the foreground (AppState 'active'/'inactive') since it was taken, or while an injected sleep-inclusive `continuousNowMs` clock covers both ends. Leaving the foreground (any non-foreground state, captured on the AppState 'change' event) ends the measurement: the reading is `authority:'floor', continuity:'unmeasured'` and `evaluateLease` returns `reconcile_required/elapsed_unmeasured` — never 'active' — until the next authenticated response re-anchors. An anchor taken outside the foreground, or when the lifecycle cannot be observed, is never measured. No native sleep-inclusive clock is assumed (none exists in the repo; `continuousNowMs` is the hook for one). Keychain calls are bounded by TRUSTED_TIME_KEYCHAIN_TIMEOUT_MS (2 s); a hung store is not re-queried in the process.

residual_risks: Any suspension (backgrounding) invalidates the measured anchor until the next authenticated response; an offline user who backgrounds the app cannot get an 'active' verdict from this module until reconnecting — this is the requested fail-closed behaviour, but the W05-04 consumer must surface a reconnection prompt rather than a silent downgrade.

`AppState.currentState` on RN can be null/undefined before the first event; such an anchor is treated as unmeasured (floor). Real-device ordering of AppState events vs. the first authenticated response is UNKNOWN from Linux.

No sleep-inclusive native clock exists in the repo; `continuousNowMs` is an injectable hook only. Providing a verified `mach_continuous_time` bridge (packages/shared-types OfflineNativeTimeEvidence) would restore offline verdicts across suspension and is future work.

TRUSTED_TIME_KEYCHAIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000 ms: a hung Keychain read delays the first read() by up to 2 s once per process (then storage='unavailable'); each later persist attempt may block the serialized queue up to 2 s at most once per checkpoint interval (60 s of trusted time).

implement.summary:
Defect on BASE_SHA (VERIFIED): there is no trusted-time module at all — `apps/mobile/src/data/trustedTime.ts` does not exist and `apps/mobile/src/data/api.ts` (request(), ~L240-300) never observes the response `Date` header — so nothing bounds a backwards wall-clock jump. Round-2 defect (VERIFIED, repro-r2-attack1.log): the r2 module (5d02b578) carried the anchor on `performance.now()` (`defaultMonotonicNowMs`, trustedTime.ts L~150) which stops during device sleep, and `trustedNow()` took `max(anchorEstimate, wall - offset)` with no notion of suspension, so backgrounding, sleeping days, winding the clock back and resuming produced authority='anchored', rollbackDetected=false and an 'active' 7-day lease after 20 real days.

Fix (c735b23d): `TrustedTimeReading.continuity` ('measured' | 'unmeasured' | 'persisted' | 'none'); `Anchor.foregroundSince` is cleared on any AppState change away from 'active'/'inactive', after which `anchorMeasured()` is false and the reading is a floor (`elapsed_unmeasured`), which `evaluateLease` never treats as active; an authenticated response taken in the foreground re-anchors as measured. Optional `continuousNowMs` (sleep-inclusive clock) restores measurement across suspension and detects the rollback/expiry when provided; when it stops answering the module falls back to the process clock conservatively. Anchors taken while backgrounded, or with `lifecycle: null` / a throwing `addEventListener`, are never measured. Wiring: `api.ts` feeds every bearer-authenticated response's `Date` header to the `trustedTime` singleton; the singleton follows RN `AppState` (checkpoint on 'active', measurement ends on leaving the foreground).

Evidence: AC1 34/34 exit 0; AC2 proof exit 0 (BASE: exit 1, suite cannot load — no module; r2 module: 12 failed/22 passed); AC3 tsc exit 0; AC4 eslint+prettier exit 0; `pnpm format:check` exit 0; `git diff --check` exit 0; wf security pin 44/44.

Adversary suite (not on this branch; round-2 file from devin/pp/w05-02/attack-5d02b578) against HEAD: 7 failed/91 passed (attack-on-r3-final.log). Of those, the two reported ATTACK 1 breaks: the 10-cycle sleep+rollback test now PASSES; the 6-day test fails at its PRECONDITION (`expect(active)` before the attack) because its lifecycle fake has no `currentState`, which this design treats as 'not known to be in the foreground' → floor. With `currentState: 'active'` added to the adversary's fake (attack-on-r3-with-currentState.log) both ATTACK 1 tests, ATTACK 2 cap-at-tolerance, ATTACK 1b forward-jump and ATTACK 7 concurrency PASS (95/98). The remaining 3 are design choices, not rollback breaks: (a) two Keychain-hang tests demand settlement within 200 ms — the module bounds hangs at 2 s (TRUSTED_TIME_KEYCHAIN_TIMEOUT_MS) and never re-asks a hung store, pinned by the new suite; (b) ATTACK 5 expects a persisted floor + honest wall clock to authorise 'active' after relaunch — this module (as in r2, judged not a break) treats a floor as a lower bound that can only prove expiry, per the fail-closed objective; W05-04 must reconcile online in that case.

implement.summary:
Defect on BASE_SHA (VERIFIED): apps/mobile has no trusted-time source at all — `src/data/trustedTime.ts` does not exist on 8ba4849d, and nothing in `src/data/api.ts` reads the authenticated `Date` header, so any offline-lease decision can only use `Date.now()` and a backwards wall-clock jump extends a lease. Prior round (r3, c735b23d) added the module but `observeServerTime()` sampled foreground state and clocks at CALL time with no notion of when the request was sent (trustedTime.ts r3 `observeServerTime`: `inForeground`/`leavesAtCall` read after resume, `anchorMs = max(serverEpochMs, anchorEstimateMs(at))`, `floor = null`) — a response in flight across a suspension re-anchored 'measured' on a days-stale Date, rewound trusted time ~6 days and revived a 7-day lease (adversary ATTACK 1a/1b).

Fix (r4): `TrustedTime.beginRequest()` returns a branded, instance-private mark recording the process/continuous clocks, foreground state and the lifecycle leave-generation at SEND time; `observeServerTime({dateHeader, authenticated, request})` treats a response as MEASURED only if a clock counted every instant of the round trip in this process (sleep-inclusive clock nondecreasing, or process clock nondecreasing with the app foregrounded throughout and no leave in between). Measured responses anchor at `max(serverEpochMs + roundTripMs, carried-forward estimate)`, re-learn the wall offset and replace the floor/mark. Everything else — no mark, foreign mark, request crossed a suspension, a clock that ran backwards — is a LOWER BOUND: it may raise the estimate and is persisted as such, but never lowers `nowMs`, never clears the persisted Keychain floor or the in-process high-water mark, never restores the previous anchor's measurement and keeps the previous wall offset (so a wound-back wall clock stays `clock_rollback`). `api.ts` marks every bearer request immediately before `fetch` and feeds `{Date header, request mark}` only after a successful, readable JSON response (auth/timeout/redirect/unreadable paths unchanged). Trusted time is now provably monotone within a process: read() pins a high-water mark, persistence is a separate device-only Keychain service (`com.picklesensei.offline.trusted-time`, AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY, cloudSync:false) bounded by a 2 s timeout, and a hung/unavailable/corrupt Keychain is reported as `storage` state, never as authorization. `evaluateLease()` caps at OFFLINE_PRO_LEASE_MAX_SECONDS and fails closed (`clock_rollback` / `elapsed_unmeasured`) whenever elapsed time cannot be measured.
